kalevalarunosong.window: c. 500 onward (ancient oral tradition; written down from 1797, recorded from 1905)
kalevalarunosong.sound: Finnic oral epic and lyric song in unrhymed, alliterative four-foot trochaic Kalevala metre, a short narrow melody repeated line after line, often sung by a lead singer answered by a second.
markers: One short melody repeated for every line of a long story
Unrhymed lines of about eight syllables, heavy alliteration
Call and response or a lead singer echoed, often unaccompanied or with kantele
near: Käppi is called a modern runo singer, but this is jouhikko-driven folk rock about a witch trial, not Kalevala-metre song
Inspired by Viena Karelian rune singers, but arranged as modern Finnish folk-pop group singing

ngoma.sound: Scope chosen: ngoma in the drum-and-dance sense in Tanzania and coastal Kenya, i.e. community dance music led by sets of tuned hand or stick drums with rattles and call-and-response singing (not the later band genres that borrowed the word).
markers: Several drums of different pitch interlocking, often a bass drum under small goblet drums
Rattles, bells or metal rings keeping a steady pulse
A lead singer answered by a dancing chorus
fits: Mashaka Kawambwa and Kitamba Kilaka with Zaramo men
near: Salum Abdallah and Cuban Marimba Band
Ngoma in the title, but early-1960s muziki wa dansi band music inspired by Cuban records; 2022 is the reissue year

amazighahwashandah.sound: Collective Amazigh village song and dance from the Atlas: two choruses answering each other in lines or circles, over frame drums (bendir/tallunt) and clapping, in Tashelhit (ahwash, High and Anti-Atlas) or Tamazight (ahidus, Middle and eastern High Atlas).
markers: Two large choruses, often men and women, singing antiphonally
Many frame drums and handclaps building interlocking, accelerating rhythms
Dancers shoulder to shoulder in a line or circle led by a central leader

cheo.sound: Northern Vietnamese village folk theatre: bright, nasal solo voices sing folk-derived melodies and comic declamation over fiddles, moon lute, flute and a small drum that sets the pace.
markers: Small chèo drum and clappers driving and punctuating each phrase
Two-string nhị fiddles, đàn nguyệt and sáo answering the singer
Switches between sung melody and half-spoken declamation (nói lệch, nói sử)
fits: Viet Nam: Hát Chèo: Traditional Folk Theatre (album)

catru.sound: Intimate northern Vietnamese sung poetry: a woman's tight, throaty, ornamented voice over the buzzing three-string đàn đáy lute, her own phách clappers and a listener's praise drum.
markers: Constricted, vibrato-laden female voice with glottal ornaments
Dry clicking phách rhythm under twangy đàn đáy lute
Occasional praise-drum strokes from a seated connoisseur
fits: Nord Việt Nam: Le Ca Trù (album)
Hanoi Ca Trù Thái Hà Ensemble
Ca Trù: The Music of North Vietnam (album)
near: Pop singer's song drawing on ca trù, not the chamber tradition itself

quanho.sound: Alternating love-song duets from the villages of Bắc Ninh: a pair of women answers a pair of men from another village, singing close, ornamented melodies that were traditionally unaccompanied and are now often staged with folk instruments.
markers: Two women answer two men in turn, the pair singing together
Dense vocal ornaments and vowel fillers (i hi, ư hư) around the lyric
Old form unaccompanied; modern staged form adds đàn nguyệt, đàn bầu, flute and fiddle
fits: Người ơi người ở đừng về
Viet Nam: Ca Tru and Quan Ho (album)

bihusongs.sound: Spring festival song of Assam: bright call-and-response love and nature verses driven by dhol, the buffalo-horn pepa, gogona and toka, now also sung on yearly Rongali Bihu albums.
markers: Dhol drumming with pepa (buffalo-horn pipe), gogona, toka and flute
Short teasing love and spring couplets, often call-and-response
Released in time for Rongali Bihu in mid-April
near: A Bihu-themed song, but made as a playback number for the film Phaguni
Assamese folk voice, but Goalpariya folk song from western Assam, not Bihu

pungmul.sound: Korean village music: loud outdoor bands of gongs and drums driving dancers in cycling rhythms, and folk songs sung with bending, sobbing voices over an hourglass drum.
markers: Small kkwaenggwari gong leading janggu, buk and jing in accelerating cycles
Swung triple-feel rhythms that speed up to a frenzy
Solo voice with wide vibrato and call-and-response refrains, as in Arirang
near: Gyeonggi folk song sung over a glam and psychedelic rock band
Chung Woong Korean Traditional Music Ensemble
Solo sung epic with drum, not a strophic folk song

huaer.window: c. 1368 onward (Ming dynasty; recorded from the 20th century)
huaer.sound: Northwest Chinese mountain love song of Gansu, Qinghai and Ningxia: a high, ringing, usually unaccompanied voice singing improvised couplets to named tunes (ling), shared by Hui, Han, Tu, Salar, Dongxiang, Bonan and Tibetan singers.
markers: One high, open-throated voice, usually unaccompanied
Tunes named as 'ling' after towns, peoples or flowers
Improvised love verses opening on a mountain or flower image
fits: Folk Music of China, Vol. 1: Folk Songs of Qinghai and Gansu (album)
Salar Zhi Ling, a folk song
near: 中央乐团小乐队, 孙丰
An instrumental chamber-orchestra arrangement of a Qinghai tune, with no singing

kulintang.sound: Gong-chime music of the Muslim southern Philippines and neighbouring islands: a row of eight small knobbed gongs plays the melody over big hanging agung gongs, gandingan gongs and a goblet drum locked in fast, driving rhythmic modes.
markers: A bright row of small kettle gongs carrying the tune
Deep hanging agung and gandingan gongs answering in a repeating pattern
Named rhythmic modes (binalig, duyog, sinulog, tidtu) driven by a single drum
fits: Danongan Kalanduyan and the Palabuniyan Kulintang Ensemble
The Music of the Magindanao in the Philippines (album)
Steven W. Otto and Usopay H. Cadar (recordists)
Muranao Kakolintang: Philippine Gong Music From Lanao, vol. 2 (album)
near: Javanese court gamelan: bronze gongs too, but slow, stately cycles with metallophones and voices, not a driving gong-row solo

malhun.window: 15th century onward (from the Tafilalt oases; later the song of Meknes, Fes, Salé, Marrakech)
malhun.sound: Moroccan sung poetry: a long strophic poem (qasida) in dialectal Arabic, sung by a lead voice with a refrain (harba) taken up between verses, over lute, violin, rebab and small drums.
markers: Long strophic poem in Moroccan dialectal Arabic, words first
A refrain (harba) answered between the verses
Lute, violin, rebab and small hand drums

garbaanddandiyaraa.sound: Gujarat's Navratri circle-dance song: devotional and Krishna songs to the Mother goddess, sung by a lead voice over dhol and clapping as dancers circle a lamp-lit pot or clash dandiya sticks.
markers: Dhol or dholak driving a looping dance beat, with handclaps or clicking sticks
Gujarati verses to Amba or about Radha and Krishna, with a short refrain
Songs run together in long non-stop medleys that speed up through the night
near: A garba staged for a Bollywood film, sung by a playback singer with a film orchestra
The 'Dandiya Queen', but this is a Hindi pop single, not a Gujarati garba

mahagita.window: 16th century onward (oldest kyo songs late Ava era; anthologised from c. 1788; standard edition 1954–61)
mahagita.sound: The Burmese court's classical song repertoire: a solo singer, usually a woman, unfolding long ornamented lines of court poetry over the arched saung harp or a small chamber ensemble, in kyo, bwe, thachingan, patpyo and Thai-derived yodaya forms.
markers: A single voice closely shadowed by the saung harp (or piano, xylophone)
Small bell and clapper (si and wa) quietly marking the cycle
Slow, restrained court poetry about kings, the Buddha, forests and longing
fits: Inle Myint Maung & Yi Yi Thant
In praise of the Burmese harp
Inle Myint Maung & Yi Yi Thant
Mahagitá: Harp and Vocal Music of Burma (album)
near: Hsaing waing orchestra of Master Sein Tin Htay
Loud outdoor drum-circle and gong-circle orchestra with oboe, the theatre ensemble rather than the intimate harp-and-voice chamber song

kobzardumy.sound: Ukrainian Cossack-era epic laments, half-sung, half-recited by blind wandering kobzari and lirnyky to their own bandura, kobza or lira (hurdy-gurdy), telling of captives in Turkish slavery, dying Cossacks and broken families.
markers: One voice with bandura, kobza or the droning lira
Free, recitative lines with no fixed verse, ending in long sighing cadences
Stories of Turkish captivity, Cossack deaths and a widow's sons
near: Russian bylina: a northern heroic epic sung without an instrument, not a Ukrainian Cossack duma

tarantella.window: c. 1600 onward (recorded from the 1950s; revival from the 1970s)
tarantella.sound: Southern Italian folk dance music in a fast, driving 6/8 or 12/8, led by frame drums with organetto, fiddle, guitar, mandolin or bagpipe, in local forms such as the Salento pizzica, the Campanian tammurriata and the tarantellas of Calabria and Montemarano.
markers: Relentless frame-drum pulse (tamburello or the big tammorra) in a fast triplet swing
Organetto, violin, mandolin or zampogna repeating short dance phrases
Dialect singing, often a solo voice and chorus, that speeds up for the dancers
near: A concert piano piece named after the dance: 6/8 virtuoso writing with no drum, dialect voice or dancers

iraqimaqam.window: c. 1600 onward (roots in Abbasid Baghdad; recorded from at least 1932)
iraqimaqam.sound: Baghdad's classical vocal suite: a lead singer (qāri') improvises long, ornate verses in a set mode against the chalghi ensemble of santur, joza spike fiddle, dumbak and daff, and each maqam ends in a lighter folk song, the pesteh.
markers: Hammered santur and scratchy joza fiddle, light hand drums
One male or female voice, long unmetred melismatic lines in classical and colloquial Arabic
A slow free maqam that breaks into a bouncy pesteh song at the end
fits: Maqam Urfa and Dishdasha Subgh il Nil
near: The pesteh that closes a maqam, sung on its own as a radio hit without the long improvised maqam before it
Irak: L'Art Du 'Ûd = The Art Of The 'Ûd (album)
Iraqi maqam modes, but instrumental oud taqsim with no singer or chalghi
